headline: Highest risk is data leakage: kotaemon’s broad egress and API-key handling can expose documents if paired with awesome-selfhosted’s content curation workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no ingestion path is documented, so direct injection into A is not evidenced. B is a web-UI RAG system that processes documents and HTML, so if A’s curated content is manually copied into B, prompt-like content could influence outputs. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies A’s content into B’s document store or chat UI
IF B is configured to treat imported text as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Keep A as read-only reference material
Paste only sanitized excerpts into B
Add a review step before importing any A-derived text
Disable any auto-ingest workflow in B
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported documents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A is a static knowledge-management resource with no network egress, while B touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and has broad egress to third-party model APIs. If A-derived material is loaded into B, B can transmit that content off-box during inference. The pairwise leakage path exists in default B configurations, though A itself does not exfiltrate.
conditions: IF A-derived documents are imported into B
IF B is configured to use any listed external API provider
mitigations: Restrict B to local-only models
Do not load sensitive A-derived files into B
Rotate any API keys used by B
Separate A reference content from B workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with B. B supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, but there is no shared writable surface with A. The only plausible conflict is operational, not capability-based, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same writable directory
IF an operator scripts shared state outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep separate directories for each agent
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Use per-agent service accounts
Check for accidental symlinked paths
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated knowledge source, and B is a support/RAG system that can render or act on retrieved content. If A’s listings or summaries are imported into B, B may treat them as authoritative without verification, creating a factual cascade. A does not itself act, but B’s downstream use of A-derived text makes the interaction plausible in default B workflows.
conditions: IF A-derived text is used as retrieval context in B
IF B is allowed to answer without source verification
mitigations: Require citations for any B answer using A content
Add a human review step for high-impact outputs
Limit B to quoted excerpts from A
Mark A content as non-authoritative reference only
requires-engineering: add verification against primary sources

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source knowledge-management site with no touched data classes, while B explicitly handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and may send them to external APIs. If regulated or secret-bearing material from B is mixed with A-derived reference content, retention and residency obligations can diverge. A is not cited for a specific residency regime, so the risk is from B’s documented handling and external transmission.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed in B
IF B uses external API providers with retention policies different from local storage
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Use a local-only deployment for B
Review vendor retention settings before upload
Separate public reference content from sensitive workspaces
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
